I will keep the land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the most practical way for me to use the full year, match the local climate, and rely on crops I know how to manage well. I do not want to spread my effort across too many crops or take market risk on something unfamiliar. I will put all 20 mu into this rotation, using improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because I care more about stable yield and easier field management than saving seed. For wheat, I will fertilize enough to support strong tillering and grain filling, irrigate at the key stages, and control weeds and disease with a limited number of spray rounds. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize on the same land, using no-tillage or very light disturbance so I do not lose moisture or miss the sowing window. For maize, I will focus on stand establishment, topdressing nitrogen, watching for borers and leaf disease, and giving water during the key growth period if rainfall is short. My goal is steady grain production, manageable labor, and lower production risk rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
